entries.title: Dear YC: Please stop downvoting thoughtful comments you disagree with.
entries.author: andreyf
entries.current_title: Dear YC: Please stop downvoting thoughtful comments you disagree with.
entries.excerpt: When someone has obviously put effort into contributing to the conversation, it's rude to downvote them to negative scores. Most recently, there some major offenders here: http://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=720779 and here: http://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=720215 and here: http://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=720569
entries.guide_zh: 作者呼吁认真写下的不同意见应得到尊重，别只因不赞同就踩到负分。

entries.guide_zh: 邀请读者介绍手头项目、工作地点，以及正在投入的事情。

entries.title: Tell HN: Please Stop Breaking HTTP Clients
entries.author: tdavis
entries.current_title: Tell HN: Please Stop Breaking HTTP Clients
entries.excerpt: For whatever ungodly reason, the news.yc web server doesn't terminate header lines properly when sending a response, which happens to break any HTTP client that actually follows the RFC. Please see RFC 2616 section 3.7.1 and use \r\n as God intended. This flexibility regarding line breaks applies only to text media in the entity-body; a bare CR or LF MUST NOT be substituted for CRLF within any of the HTTP control structures (such as header fields and multipart boundaries). entries.guide_zh: 作者报告 HN 的 HTTP 响应头换行问题，称它会破坏合规客户端。

entries.title: Ask HN: Why Python over Ruby?
entries.author: costan
entries.current_title: Ask HN: Why Python over Ruby?
entries.excerpt: I would like to understand why Python is so much more popular than Ruby. Much of the software I've seen supports Python for scripting (e.g. Miro, OpenMoko, XBMC/Boxee), and people don't seem to care so much for Ruby. At the same time, people agree that Ruby is great for writing DSLs. I don't want a flame war or religious arguments. I would like to understand what made Python win in this space. Thanks so much for commenting!
entries.guide_zh: 为何嵌入式脚本等场景常支持 Python，却较少选择 Ruby？

entries.title: You will live for longer than 1% of the entire history of human civilization.
entries.author: GraffitiTim
entries.current_title: You will live for longer than 1% of the entire history of human civilization.
entries.excerpt: The first civilization started in Mesopotamia around 5000 BCE (more or less), which is 7,000 years ago. If you live until age 80, that's more than 1% of the history of civilization. Just throwing it out there for anyone else who'd never thought about it before. Certainly changed my perspective a bit.
entries.guide_zh: 作者用个人寿命占文明史的比例，提醒读者换个尺度看待时间。

entries.title: Ask HN: Cash-flow muses
entries.author: bkovitz
entries.excerpt: Timothy "Four-Hour Work Week" Ferriss has a concept he calls a "cash-flow muse". That's a little business that generates some monthly cash without taking up too much of your time. I think the idea is that with a couple of these running, you're pretty much free to do as you please most of the time. Some desirable attributes of a cash-flow muse: - You own it. - The value proposition is simple enough to explain in one sentence. - High margin: 4x to 50x. - Easy to automate or out
entries.guide_zh: 有没有无需持续投入大量时间、却能带来稳定现金流的小生意？
